case.summary: Case HHG-013 involves an online card-not-present transaction initiated from a new Windows device running Chrome, triggering a `card_not_present_new_device` pattern with a low calibrated fraud probability of 0.06. While the history reveals prior confirmed fraud cases on both this card tuple and a different card, along with a top-decile risk score and online channel usage, the new device flag historically aligns more frequently with benign events like travel or new phones rather than actual fraud. Similar historical cases such as CC-3475, CC-2367, and CC-0852 demonstrate that high-risk alerts can successfully clear when legitimate customer activity—such as travel—is verified. Weighing these behavioral indicators and historical precedents, the policy engine ultimately determined that the alert should be closed as legitimate. Consequently, the decided action for this case is CLOSE_NO_FRAUD, meaning no further restrictions or verifications will be applied to the transaction.
